title: Wildfire smoke and air-quality welfare check
purpose: check that a person with breathing or heart conditions is safe during heavy smoke and find out if they need help
questions: Are you indoors with the windows closed, and do you have a fan, air conditioner or air purifier running?
Do you have your inhaler or breathing medication with you, and enough of it?
Are you coughing more than usual, wheezing, short of breath, or feeling chest tightness?
Is there anything you need: a mask, your medication, a ride to a clean-air centre, or someone to come by?
confusion_probe: If the person seems confused or disoriented, gently ask once: Can you tell me what day it is today?
red_flags: out of breathing medication with symptoms
advice: Stay indoors, keep windows and doors closed, and run air conditioning on recirculate if you have it.
Use your prescribed inhaler as directed by your doctor.
red_flag_instruction: If breathing is difficult or there is chest pain, tell the person calmly to call {{emergency_number}} now and that you are alerting their emergency contact. Do not adjust any medication dose.
voicemail_message: This is an automated welfare call from {{org}} because of heavy smoke in your area. Please stay indoors with windows closed and call {{emergency_number}} if breathing becomes difficult. We will try again shortly.

escalation_reason_templates.red: reported breathing problems during our smoke welfare call: {{reasons}}
escalation_reason_templates.unreachable: could not be reached by phone after {{attempts}} attempts during the smoke event
escalation_reason_templates.unverified: answered but we could not confirm they are safe
